cohort: The study included 60,078 deliveries from surveillance sites in rural Bangladesh, India, and Makwanpur and Dhanusha districts in Nepal.
finding: Socioeconomic inequalities in newborn care were observed across all study sites, with literate mothers having higher facility delivery rates and better newborn care scores.
mod_finding: Use of facility delivery was higher among literate mothers, and adjusting for place of delivery (home vs. facility) reduced the effect of literacy on the newborn care score, indicating its role in socioeconomic inequalities.
